players.product: AI colocation in retrofit data centers (NC-1 North Carolina 40 MW IT leased to Nscale; MTL-3 Montreal for Cerebras) plus GPU cloud services on NVIDIA B300 / Vera Rubin clusters

quarterly_data.signal: WhiteFiber's June 2026 investor presentation (company information as of May 31, 2026; gross MW): ~11 MW online in 2025, ~76 MW online by YE 2026E, a ~1.5 GW data center pipeline, ~5,000 NVIDIA GPUs contracted and 20+ customers; MTL-1 (4 MW) is fully occupied by 14 customers and development of MTL-2 (5 MW) had been put on hold. Retrofit buildout cost is ~$8M to $10M per gross MW (MTL-3: under C$9M per MW, PUE 1.3, delivered in ~6 months). At NC-1 Duke Energy has completed the work to deliver the initial 54 gross MW of utility power, with an energy cost of ~$0.05 per kWh.
quarterly_data.figure: ~76 MW online by YE 2026E; ~1.5 GW pipeline; ~5,000 NVIDIA GPUs contracted; NC-1 initial 54 gross MW of utility power

quarterly_data.signal: WhiteFiber's June 2026 presentation, first quarter 2026 results: total revenues $21,923,451 versus $16,767,516 a year earlier; cloud services $16,766,543 versus $14,842,286 and colocation services $4,773,550 versus $1,644,663; adjusted EBITDA $3,001,474 versus $5,990,096.

connects_to.relationship: NC-1 (North Carolina) AI colocation: 40 MW of IT load leased to Nscale under a 10-year agreement

contracts.signal: WhiteFiber's June 2026 presentation: the NC-1 agreement with Nscale is a modified gross lease with expense pass-through; Nscale receives priority notification rights for future site capacity, with potential expansion toward ~2x the initial deployment by end of 2027; project-level financing is expected to support the remaining deployment.
